# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist + Timeline

---

## DECLUTTER PRINCIPLES (read once, apply everywhere)

Before packing any room, run everything through this quick filter. It takes about 10 minutes per room before you start and saves hours of moving things you'll just throw out later.

**Keep** if you've used it in the last 12 months, it has clear sentimental value, or it's expensive to replace.

**Donate** if it's in good condition but hasn't been used, doesn't fit, or duplicates something else you own.

**Sell** if it has real resale value. Use Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist for furniture and large items; eBay for electronics and collectibles. Don't spend more than 30 minutes listing something — if it doesn't sell in a week, donate it.

**Trash/Recycle** if it's broken, stained, missing parts, or not worth anyone's time.

**Oregon Rule:** Moving cross-country costs roughly $0.50–$1.50 per pound with a truck or mover. If an item costs less than that to replace and you don't love it, leave it behind.

---

## WEEK-BY-WEEK PACKING TIMELINE

You have 10 weeks. Packing starts in earnest around Week 6 and intensifies from Week 4 onward. Weeks 1–5 are for decisions and supplies, not boxes.

**Week 10–8 (now — Deciding and Acquiring)**
Focus on decluttering decisions, not packing. Walk every room once with a trash bag and a donate box. Order or collect supplies. **J, ~3–4 hrs total.**

**Week 7–6 (Supplies ready, start non-essentials)**
Pack storage areas: garage, basement, attic, storage unit, holiday decorations, sports equipment, tools you won't need before the move. These spaces tend to be the most cluttered and benefit most from a hard declutter pass. **J, ~4–6 hrs per large space.**

**Week 5–4 (Secondary rooms)**
Pack the guest room completely. Pack books, art, décor, and anything decorative throughout the house. Pack off-season clothes. Pack the office (except daily-use items). Pack the living room except the couch, TV, and one lamp. **J, ~2–3 hrs per room.**

**Week 3 (Kitchen and dining)**
Pack 80% of the kitchen: duplicates, rarely used appliances, baking equipment, most pantry items. Leave out enough to cook simple meals for 2–3 weeks. Use up pantry food aggressively. **J, ~3–4 hrs.**

**Week 2 (Bedrooms, bathrooms, final push)**
Pack bedrooms down to sleeping essentials (one set of sheets, towels, toiletries). Pack bathrooms except daily-use items. Pack remaining living room items. Mark all boxes clearly. **J, ~2–3 hrs per room.**

**Week 1 (Essentials only)**
Everything remaining fits in your overnight bags, the moving-day essentials box, and the dog bag. Fridge gets emptied and defrosted 24 hrs before movers or truck pickup. **J, ~2–3 hrs.**

---

## ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING CHECKLIST

Each room has three sections: **Declutter first**, **Pack early** (weeks 6–4), and **Pack last** (weeks 2–1). The "Last Out" box for each room stays unpacked until moving day and goes in the car or is loaded last on the truck, clearly labeled.

---

### KITCHEN — J, ~3–4 hrs to pack fully

**Declutter first:**
Toss expired pantry items. Donate duplicate gadgets (how many spatulas do you need in Oregon?). Discard mismatched containers missing lids. If you haven't used an appliance in a year, seriously consider leaving it. Small appliances are heavy and cheap to replace.

**Pack early (weeks 5–3):**
- Baking sheets, muffin tins, cake pans
- Rarely used appliances: stand mixer, waffle iron, bread maker, juicer
- Extra sets of dishes or glasses (pack one full set last)
- Cookbooks
- Pantry: canned goods, dry goods, spices (use up what you can; donate the rest to a food bank)
- Vases, serving platters, decorative items
- Bar tools, holiday entertaining items

**Pack last (week 2–1):**
- One pot, one pan, one baking dish
- Enough dishes and glasses for two (wrap carefully)
- Knives and cutting board
- Coffee maker or kettle
- Daily-use utensils
- Dish soap, sponge, hand towel

**Last Out box label: KITCHEN — OPEN FIRST**
Include: paper plates and cups, coffee supplies, one pot, two mugs, utensils, dish soap, sponge, one roll of paper towel.

---

### LIVING ROOM — J, ~2–3 hrs

**Declutter first:**
Donate books you won't reread (be honest). Recycle old magazines. Part with decorative items you don't love. Assess furniture: some pieces cost more to move than to replace.

**Pack early (weeks 6–4):**
- All books
- Art and wall décor (wrap frames in clothing or bubble wrap)
- Throw pillows, extra blankets
- Board games, puzzles, DVDs, gaming accessories
- Candles, vases, decorative objects
- Shelving contents

**Pack last (week 2–1):**
- TV and cables (label every cable with tape and a marker before unplugging)
- One lamp (if the new place won't have overhead lighting immediately)
- Remote controls

**Last Out box:** TV remotes and cables, one power strip, your laptop charger.

---

### PRIMARY BEDROOM — J, ~2–3 hrs

**Declutter first:**
One pass through every drawer and shelf. Donate clothes you haven't worn in 12 months. Be especially ruthless with duplicates (10 t-shirts becomes 6). Same rule for shoes. Discard or donate any bedding you won't use.

**Pack early (weeks 5–4):**
- Off-season clothing (pack by person, label clearly)
- Extra bedding (keep one set per person out)
- Books on nightstands
- Jewelry and accessories except daily-use items
- Décor, frames, art

**Pack last (week 2–1):**
- Current-season clothing (leave out a week's worth per person)
- One set of sheets and pillows per person
- Toiletry organizers (transfer to toiletry bag week 1)
- Alarm clock or charger

**Last Out box:** One set of sheets, two pillows, phone chargers, one change of clothes per person.

---

### GUEST ROOM / SPARE ROOM — P or J, ~1–2 hrs

This room gets packed first (week 6–7) since nothing in it is daily-use.

**Declutter first:**
If the guest room has become a storage room, treat it as such — this is where the most ruthless decluttering happens.

**Pack everything:**
- All bedding and linens
- Stored clothing
- Holiday items and seasonal décor
- Hobby supplies, craft materials, instruments
- Luggage (pack smaller bags inside larger ones; use the inside of luggage to pack soft items)
- Books, games, whatever else has ended up in here

---

### BATHROOMS (Primary and Guest) — M or J, ~1–2 hrs total

**Declutter first:**
Toss expired medications (use an Ohio DEA take-back program or a pharmacy — don't flush). Toss expired makeup, skincare, and hair products. Donate duplicates. Be realistic about what you actually use.

**Pack early (weeks 5–4):**
- Extra towels and washcloths (keep 2 sets out)
- Hair tools you don't use daily
- First aid kit (pack it, but note which box it's in)
- Cleaning supplies (most can be replaced cheaply — check whether movers will transport them; many won't take flammables or bleach)

**Pack last (week 1):**
- Daily-use toiletries
- Medication (carry prescriptions with you in the car, not on the truck)
- Two towels per person
- Toilet paper (leave a half-roll out until literally the last moment)
- Shower curtain and liner

**Last Out box / Overnight bag:** Toiletries, prescriptions, 2 towels, one roll of toilet paper. These go in the car.

---

### HOME OFFICE — M or P (whoever uses it), ~2–3 hrs

**Declutter first:**
Shred documents you don't need (shred anything with personal data). Recycle old cables that go to nothing. Donate books, binders, and equipment you no longer use. Assess furniture — office desks and chairs are heavy and inexpensive on Facebook Marketplace.

**Pack early (weeks 6–5):**
- Books and binders
- File boxes and archives
- Printer and extra toner
- Monitors (wrap well; use original box if you have it)
- Extra peripherals and cables (label before packing)
- Art and décor

**Pack last (week 2):**
- Daily-use laptop, charger, mouse, keyboard
- Current files and notebooks
- Any external hard drives or USB drives (carry in the car)

**Critical:** All hard drives, flash drives, important physical documents, and backup drives go in the car. Not the truck.

---

### GARAGE / BASEMENT / STORAGE — J, ~4–6 hrs per large space (start week 7)

This is your biggest declutter opportunity. The rule here is simple: if you couldn't tell someone what it is or when you last used it, donate or trash it.

**Declutter hard:**
Power tools you haven't used in 2 years. Duplicate gardening tools. Sporting equipment for sports you don't play. Random hardware (keep one good toolkit, donate the rest). Old paint (most movers won't take it; check Oregon's hazardous waste program for disposal at the new end, and Ohio's for disposal now).

**Pack:**
- Neatly boxed tools with labels
- Sports equipment you'll actually use
- Holiday decor (clearly labeled by holiday)
- Camping and outdoor gear
- Bike (may need partial disassembly for the truck)
- Garden hoses and hand tools worth keeping

**Don't move:**
Propane tanks, gas cans, paint cans, aerosol cans, fertilizer, pesticides, pool chemicals, fire extinguishers. Dispose of properly before the move. Check FMCSA rules — these are prohibited on moving trucks by regulation.

---

### DOG'S STUFF — M, ~1 hr

**Keep accessible (goes in the car, not the truck):**
- Food and treats (at least 3–4 days' worth)
- Water and collapsible travel bowl
- Leash, harness, collar with current ID tag
- Crate or travel bed (familiar scent helps with anxiety)
- Favorite toy or blanket
- Poop bags
- Medications and vet records
- Paper towels and cleaner (car accidents happen)
- Dog first aid kit basics

**Pack early:** Extra crates, beds, or pet furniture. Extra bags of food if you're stocked.

---

### GENERAL PACKING TIPS

Label every box with its destination room, a brief contents description, and a priority: **Open First**, **Normal**, or **Storage**. Mark fragile boxes on all four sides, not just the top. Pack heavy items in small boxes (books, canned goods). Pack light items in large boxes (linens, pillows). Don't leave empty space in boxes — fill gaps with clothing, towels, or packing paper so boxes don't collapse. Take a photo of the inside of each box before closing if you're anxious about contents.

---

# Moving Day Essentials — Complete One-Pager

---

## PRINT INSTRUCTIONS
**Letter (8.5×11"):** Set margins to 0.5" all around. Font: Arial or Helvetica 9pt body, 11pt headers. Should fit on one page printed front-and-back, or one page single-sided at 85% scale.
**A4:** Same margins and font. Scale to 90% if needed. Fold in thirds to fit a glove box.
**Laminate if possible** — it'll survive the whole move.

---

---

# ✅ MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS
### Ohio → Oregon · Keep this in the car

---

## 📁 DOCUMENTS ENVELOPE *(J — assemble night before, 20 min)*
- [ ] Driver's licenses, both
- [ ] Passports (if you have them)
- [ ] Vehicle title, registration, insurance card
- [ ] New lease or purchase closing paperwork
- [ ] Moving contract + Bill of Lading + inventory list
- [ ] Mover's phone number and driver's cell
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt + carrier contact (if shipping)
- [ ] Dog: rabies certificate, vaccine records, microchip number, vet contact
- [ ] Both prescriptions + a 2-week supply of all medications
- [ ] Social Security cards + birth certificates (or copies)
- [ ] New landlord/property manager contact info
- [ ] Emergency contacts list (printed, not just in your phone)

---

## 🐕 DOG BAG *(M — pack night before, 30 min)*
- [ ] Food + treats (3–4 days' supply)
- [ ] Water jug + collapsible bowl
- [ ] Leash, harness, collar with current ID tag
- [ ] Crate or travel bed with a familiar blanket or shirt
- [ ] Favorite toy
- [ ] Poop bags (more than you think you need)
- [ ] Medications + dosing notes
- [ ] Paper towels + enzymatic cleaner (car accidents happen)
- [ ] Dog first aid basics: gauze, antiseptic wipe, tweezers

---

## 🧳 OVERNIGHT BAG — EACH PERSON *(M + P — pack night before, 20 min each)*
- [ ] 2–3 days of clothes + one nice outfit (for surprises)
- [ ] Toiletries: toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, face wash, shampoo
- [ ] Medications (carry-on only, never on the truck)
- [ ] Phone + laptop chargers
- [ ] Earbuds or headphones
- [ ] Glasses, contacts + solution
- [ ] Small snack supply for the road

---

## 📦 OPEN-FIRST BOX *(J — load last on truck or in car trunk, 15 min)*
- [ ] Paper plates, cups, plastic utensils
- [ ] Coffee supplies + one mug per person
- [ ] One pot or kettle
- [ ] Dish soap + sponge + 2 paper towels rolls
- [ ] Toilet paper (at least 4 rolls)
- [ ] Hand soap
- [ ] One set of sheets per person + 2 pillows
- [ ] 2 towels per person
- [ ] Shower curtain + liner + rings
- [ ] Basic toolkit: hammer, screwdriver, box cutter, Allen wrench set
- [ ] Extension cord + power strip
- [ ] Trash bags (a full roll)
- [ ] Scissors + markers + tape
- [ ] Small first aid kit: bandages, ibuprofen, antacid

---

## 🚗 CAR EMERGENCY KIT *(M — check night before, 15 min)*
- [ ] Jumper cables or jump starter pack
- [ ] Tire inflator / fix-a-flat
- [ ] Flashlight + extra batteries
- [ ] Reflective triangles or road flares
- [ ] Basic tool kit (tire iron, duct tape, zip ties)
- [ ] Extra engine oil + coolant (1 qt each)
- [ ] Paper map or downloaded offline maps (cell service gets thin in rural Oregon)
- [ ] Reusable water bottles, filled
- [ ] Non-perishable snacks: nuts, bars, jerky
- [ ] Blanket (useful even in summer in the mountains)
- [ ] Phone mount + car charger + backup battery pack
- [ ] Cash — $200 minimum (some rural gas stations and tips for movers)

---

## ☑️ BEFORE YOU LEAVE — FINAL WALK-THROUGH *(J — 30 min)*
- [ ] Photo/video of every room, closet, and outside — timestamped
- [ ] Photo of all utility meters (gas, electric, water)
- [ ] All windows closed and locked
- [ ] All lights off, fans off, HVAC set or off
- [ ] All appliances unplugged (check the garage too)
- [ ] Fridge emptied and door left slightly open
- [ ] Nothing left in cabinets, closets, attic, garage, storage
- [ ] Keys, fobs, garage remotes, mailbox key returned — get a receipt or photo confirmation
- [ ] Bill of Lading reviewed and signed — do NOT sign blank or incomplete forms
- [ ] Mover's final inventory checked against your copy
- [ ] Dog secured in car before movers start carrying things out

---

## 📍 DRIVE-DAY REMINDERS *(M drives, P navigates or swap)*
- [ ] Leave early — aim for a 7–8 AM start
- [ ] Dog break every 2–3 hours minimum
- [ ] Never leave dog in a parked car (heat rises fast, even at 65°F)
- [ ] Log mileage at start and end of each day (reimbursement/tax records)
- [ ] Keep Bill of Lading and mover contact accessible throughout the drive
- [ ] Text your new landlord or property manager your ETA when you're 1 day out
- [ ] Check in with the mover's driver daily to confirm delivery window

---

## 🔑 ARRIVAL — FIRST 30 MINUTES *(J — 30 min)*
- [ ] Photo/video of new place before anything is unloaded — note any existing damage
- [ ] Locate: water shutoff, breaker box, gas shutoff
- [ ] Confirm utilities are on (lights, hot water, heat/AC)
- [ ] Put dog somewhere safe and calm — a bathroom with their bed works well
- [ ] Unload the Open-First box before anything else
- [ ] Confirm renter's insurance is active (if not done yet, do it from your phone now)
